templates.name_en: Grip, briefly lift, and release a mug within its starting area
templates.name_ja: マグカップを把持し、少し持ち上げて同じ開始位置に戻す

templates.name_en: Reach to and pull an upright wine glass along the tabletop
templates.name_ja: テーブル上のワイングラスに手を伸ばし、立てたまま手前へ引く

tasks.name_en: Grip and release the mug within its marked starting area
tasks.name_ja: マグカップを把持し、印の範囲内で放す
instruction_variants: If you choose, pick up the empty mug, lift it just clear of the tabletop, and set it back within its marked starting area.
Optionally grip the empty mug, briefly lift it, then release it upright inside the marked starting area.
よろしければ、空のマグカップを持ち上げ、テーブルの印の範囲内に戻して放してください。
tasks.notes: Optional, neutral interaction proposal whose observable events are mug pickup/grasp, brief clearance from the surface, release, and final pose within the original marked area. It is scoped to handling rather than carrying the mug to a different location, reflecting the WHO ICF d440 definition and its exclusion for lifting and carrying (d430). The ICF code classifies a functioning domain; it does not prescribe this task or a procedure. Do not infer ability, disability, diagnosis, or accommodation outcome from participation or performance.

tasks.name_en: Reach to and pull the wine glass toward the near marked area
tasks.name_ja: ワイングラスに手を伸ばし、手前の印まで引き寄せる
instruction_variants: If you choose, reach to the empty wine glass at the far mark and pull it along the tabletop to the near mark, keeping it upright.
Optionally move the empty wine glass from the far tabletop mark to the near mark by pulling it without lifting it.
よろしければ、空のワイングラスを立てたまま、テーブル上で奥の印から手前の印まで引き寄せてください。
tasks.notes: Optional, neutral interaction proposal with observable reaching/contact, pulling displacement, release, and final stability. Its d445 relation is a curator mapping to the WHO definition and listed pulling/reaching activities, not an ICF-prescribed procedure or exclusive classification; the action can involve fine hand use as well. Do not infer ability, disability, diagnosis, or accommodation outcome from participation or performance.

requirements.reason: The tabletop supplies a stable starting surface and clearly marked return area.
Reusable YCB drinkware object instance; its use here is a proposed interaction mapping.
An empty vessel avoids making liquid handling part of the proposed primitive.
The return footprint makes final placement observable without requiring transfer to another location.
The setup should not add unrelated obstacles to the optional handling interaction.

success_criteria: If the participant opts in, record whether pickup/grasp and release events occurred, and whether the mug ended upright and stable within its original marked area.
Do not score or label the result as a measure of an individual's ability or disability.
setup: Offer the interaction as optional and explain what interaction data would be recorded before any recording begins.
Place one empty YCB mug upright within a visible tabletop start-area outline; keep the short lift-and-return area clear.
reset: Return the empty mug upright to the marked start area and confirm that the area is clear.
quality_checks: Record only task events and final object pose needed to describe this setup; do not infer clinical status, ability, or accommodation outcome.
Confirm that the mug did not need to travel to another location; if carrying is introduced, treat that as a changed task scope.

requirements.reason: The task is scoped to a clear tabletop surface with two visible marked zones.
Reusable YCB drinkware object instance; its use here is a proposed interaction mapping.
An empty vessel avoids making liquid handling part of the proposed primitive.
Distinct zones make reaching direction and tabletop displacement observable.
The wine glass is intended to remain supported by the surface throughout the pull.

success_criteria: If the participant opts in, record whether reaching/contact and a pull toward the near mark occurred, and whether the glass ended upright and stable in that zone.
Do not score or label the result as a measure of an individual's ability or disability.
setup: Offer the interaction as optional and explain what interaction data would be recorded before any recording begins.
Place one empty YCB wine glass upright at the far tabletop mark; keep the surface path to the near mark clear.
reset: Return the empty wine glass upright to the far mark and confirm that the path and target area are clear.
quality_checks: Record the interaction and final object pose only; do not infer clinical status, ability, or accommodation outcome.
Confirm that the glass remained supported by the tabletop; lifting or carrying would change this proposed scope.

evidence.source_name: WHO ICF Browser: d440 Fine hand use
evidence.scope: The WHO definition describes coordinated handling of objects by hand, fingers, and thumb, including picking up, manipulating, and releasing; its inclusion list includes picking up, grasping, manipulating, and releasing. It excludes lifting and carrying objects (d430).
evidence.limitations: The ICF code classifies a functioning domain; it does not prescribe a task, test, procedure, robot action, or participant outcome. The source does not support prevalence, individual ability/disability/diagnosis, accommodation outcome, robot execution, or asset compatibility. The Atlas task is only a proposed optional interaction mapping, deliberately limited to brief pickup and return within the same marked area.
evidence.notes: Primary WHO classification entry. Official URL: https://apps.who.int/classifications/icfbrowser/Browse.aspx?code=d440.

evidence.source_name: WHO ICF Browser: d445 Hand and arm use
evidence.scope: The WHO definition describes coordinated hand-and-arm actions to move or manipulate objects, and lists pulling/pushing, reaching, and turning/twisting among inclusions.
evidence.limitations: The ICF code classifies a functioning domain; it does not prescribe a task, test, procedure, robot action, or participant outcome. The source does not support prevalence, individual ability/disability/diagnosis, accommodation outcome, robot execution, or asset compatibility. The tabletop wine-glass pull is an Atlas proposal mapped to pulling/reaching, not a WHO-defined task, and it may also involve fine hand use.
evidence.notes: Primary WHO classification entry. Official URL: https://apps.who.int/classifications/icfbrowser/Browse.aspx?code=d445&hsr=1.

The WHO ICF d440 and d445 codes classify functioning domains and describe activity categories. They do not prescribe tasks, clinical tests, or robot procedures. These interactions are curator-authored, optional collection-design proposals. Do not infer participant ability, disability, diagnosis, or accommodation outcome, and do not report participation or performance as clinical measurement.

Use only the source-supported proposal-level task_suitability claims. Population frequency, robot execution, asset compatibility, timing, and clinical interpretation remain unknown. All duration estimates are null.
